issue.title: Refuse a merge the wrapper cannot see, and test both copies of merge-pr.mjs

repository.name: b-fac
repository.description: Harness-agnostic agent factory: the orchestrated-delivery workflow as a portable plugin/skill

issue.body:
Closes #200

Both copies of `merge-pr.mjs` now have tests, and the shipped copy no longer merges when it cannot tell whether a branch is behind its base. ADR 0063 records the decision, and which of the remaining differences between the copies are configuration and which are behaviour.

## Functionality

**What the premise got right, and where it went further.** The fail-open was real, and it had three causes, not one:

1. **Every fork PR.** The compare asked about the head by branch *name*, which a fork's branch does not have in the base repository. I measured this on a public fork PR, cli/cli#14519: `compare/trunk...document-search-operator-support` returned **404**, `compare/trunk...<headRefOid>` returned **0**, and `compare/trunk...waldyrious:<branch>` returned **0**. Under the old code, every fork PR skipped the refusal.
2. **Any `gh` error.**
3. **An empty answer.** `Number('')` is `0`, so an empty answer read as "not behind" and got past the `NaN` test.

It also turned up a fork defect the issue did not name. After a merge the wrapper runs `DELETE refs/heads/<headRefName>` in the *base* repository. For a fork PR opened from the fork's own `main`, that deletes the base repository's `main` wherever nothing protects it, which is the setup the asset is written for.

**Decision on a null lookup: refuse** (while `REFUSE_WHEN_BEHIND` is on). The refusal prints the `gh` error and the exact `gh api` call, so the operator can rerun it by hand. Asking by head SHA is what keeps this from costing fork PRs every merge. The remaining cost falls on the maintainer: a dead token, no network or a rate limit is now a hard stop instead of a warning. Only a public fork was measured.

**What I ran:**

- `node --test scripts/merge-pr.test.mjs`: 58 tests, all passing. The shared suite runs 27 cases against each copy, and 4 more are copy-specific.
- **Mutation check.** I put each of the four defects back into the asset, one at a time, and reran the suite. Each one turned it red: fail-open on null (9 tests), compare by name (5), deleting a fork's branch (3), and an empty answer read as 0 (3).
- `node scripts/merge-pr.mjs` with no argument prints usage and exits 1. `node scripts/merge-pr.mjs 207` refused with "state is MERGED" and exit 1.
- **Read-only dry run of the real module against real `gh`, with `PUT` and `DELETE` intercepted.** Results are in the comment below.
- `npm run check` is green, with 990 tests. `check:plugin` and `check:plugin-load` are green, and `check:version` reports 0.54.5 → 0.54.6 (rebased onto #208, which took 0.54.5 and ADR 0062, so this ADR is 0063).

**Not done:** I did not open an interactive `claude --plugin-dir .` session. The skill change is one paragraph in `references/enforcement.md`, layer 1, and I read it in the file.

## Code

`run({ prNumber, gh, sleep, log, warn, error, required, refuseWhenBehind })` returns an exit code instead of calling `process.exit`. The entry-point check is the same one `post-body.mjs` uses. The body is identical in both copies, except for three things:

- `REQUIRED`'s values
- comments
- this repository's WHAT JUST SHIPPED block

`REQUIRED` stays a column-0 `const` because `check-setup.mjs` reads it with `^const REQUIRED = \[`.

The two copies used to differ in about 60 lines of code. Now they differ in the `REQUIRED` line and the release block, and nothing else.

The `staleRefusal` message adds the HTTP 405 sentence only when GitHub reports `BEHIND`, which is the one case where that sentence is true.

## Architecture

- **No new pattern.** The injected-`gh`, importable shape is taken from `post-body.mjs`. One test file covering two copies follows the precedent of `command-reader.test.mjs`.
- **New ADR 0063.** It holds the null decision, the SHA compare, the fork-delete fix, and a table that sorts every remaining difference into configuration, behaviour or prose.
- **This repository's copy gains `REFUSE_WHEN_BEHIND = true`.** Here it is redundant with the ruleset, and deliberately so: it is the only place the logic gets exercised before a stranger trusts it.
- **Payload changed:** the asset and `references/enforcement.md`. The version goes to 0.54.6, as briefed.
- **Out of scope, left alone:** the guard files, and #205.

message:
Document search operator support in `gh search` help

The `--help` output of `gh search issues` and `gh search prs`
lacked information on using boolean operators (`OR`, `AND`)
and parentheses for nesting. Each operator must be passed as separate arguments;
wrapping a whole query string in quotes makes it match as a single literal phrase,
so the operators are treated as plain words,
and the search will fail to capture relevant results
rather than reporting usage of unsupported syntax.

This patch updates the help text to make this nuance explicit to users.

issue.title: Deliver inline pull request review comments and thread replies to the session

repository.name: simple-software-factory
repository.description: Make GitHub the place where your AI agents collaborate with each other and you.

issue.body:
🤖#591 claude/claude-fable-5-1/medium (17% of 1M) says: <!-- ssf: origin=mikekelly/simple-software-factory#591 -->

## Outcome
Inline pull request review comments and review-thread replies are delivered to the session like any other activity.

## Problem
ssf reads only `issues/{n}/timeline` ([github.rs](https://github.com/mikekelly/simple-software-factory/blob/a0ef619/src/github.rs#L828-L872)). GitHub's timeline does not carry `pulls/{n}/comments`: on cli/cli#14519 there are 16 review comments and zero `line-commented` timeline events. A "changes requested" review with an empty body arrives as `reviewed (changes_requested)` and the actual requests are lost; thread replies never arrive. The [`line-commented` renderer](https://github.com/mikekelly/simple-software-factory/blob/a0ef619/src/prompt/timeline.rs#L282) and its tests use a shape the API does not send, and [docs/internals.md](https://github.com/mikekelly/simple-software-factory/blob/a0ef619/docs/internals.md#L122) overstates what is delivered. `gh pr view --comments` does not print these either (verified), so agents cannot work around it without `gh api`.

## Acceptance
- On pull requests, also list `pulls/{n}/comments` (conditional, `since=`), keyed by comment id with `updated_at` as the edit marker, merged into the diff and allow-checked like other events.
- Until then, the review-request prompt tells the agent to run `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/comments`.
- Description edits, review-body edits and deleted comments are delivered or explicitly documented as not delivered.
- Docs corrected.

Refs #591 (CTO audit, finding 4). Priority tier 2: preserve feedback.

issue.title: Remove host versions from `gh project item-list` help
issue.body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!

If you are proposing a fix for a security issue, STOP and follow .github/SECURITY.md instead.

Keep the entire pull request self-contained, reviewer-facing, and diegetic: describe the
change, rationale, and evidence within the context of the repository and pull request. Do not
narrate how the pull request was produced or refer to private conversations, prior agent work,
or other behind-the-scenes context. Omit those details unless they materially affect review;
if they do, state the relevant fact and its significance directly.
-->

<!-- List related issues here. Use `fixes` or `closes` keywords to associate an issue number. -->

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

The help for `gh project item-list` names the hosts that support `--query`. That list is already incomplete: it leaves out GHE.com, where `gh` also allows `--query`. Its GHES version will also go stale as older releases age out. Which hosts support a feature is better left to the GitHub docs.

This drops the host list from the [`item-list` help text](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/0706fa4d513426c0961720732198d6e0f7b54cdd/pkg/cmd/project/item-list/item_list.go#L44-L46) and keeps the rest of the sentence:

```diff
-If supported by the API host (github.com and GHES 3.20+), the --query option can
-be used to perform advanced search. For the full syntax, see:
+If supported by the API host, the --query option can be used to perform
+advanced search. For the full syntax, see:
```

It also removes an extra blank line that #14519 added to the [`search issues` help text](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/0706fa4d513426c0961720732198d6e0f7b54cdd/pkg/cmd/search/issues/issues.go#L37-L38).

### How did you test this change?

<!--
Report only actions you actually performed and results you actually observed, using factual
first-person language (for example, "I ran..." and "I saw..."). Do not present planned,
hypothetical, inferred, or merely expected scenarios as testing.

Automated test results do not belong here. Passing unit tests, `go test ./...` output, and
coverage numbers tell a reviewer nothing they cannot see from CI, so do not paste them.

If you did not exercise the changed behavior, write `Not tested` and explain why.

Use one or more of these, whichever communicates best:

1. Screenshots or GIFs of the real command running. Preferred whenever the change is visible
   in terminal output. If output changed, show it before and after.
2. Given/When/Then scenarios, but only when you actually executed the steps. For example:
   Given I was in a repo with no open pull requests
   When I ran `gh pr list`
   Then I saw "no open pull requests in cli/cli"
3. A natural language walkthrough of what you did by hand, the states you covered, and what
   you saw, including error and edge cases.

If you leave this empty, your pull request will very likely be closed.
-->

I built one binary from trunk and one from this branch. I ran `gh project item-list --help` and `gh search issues --help` with each.

`gh project item-list --help` before:

```text
List the items in a project.

If supported by the API host (github.com and GHES 3.20+), the --query option can
be used to perform advanced search. For the full syntax, see:
https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/customizing-views-in-your-project/filtering-projects
```

After:

```text
List the items in a project.

If supported by the API host, the --query option can be used to perform
advanced search. For the full syntax, see:
https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/customizing-views-in-your-project/filtering-projects
```

`gh search issues --help` before, with two blank lines after the first paragraph:

```text
The command supports constructing queries using the GitHub search syntax,
using the parameter and qualifier flags, or a combination of the two.


GitHub search syntax is documented at:
```

After, with one:

```text
The command supports constructing queries using the GitHub search syntax,
using the parameter and qualifier flags, or a combination of the two.

GitHub search syntax is documented at:
```

### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

- Users on a host without `--query` support still get a clear error. [`runList`](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/0706fa4d513426c0961720732198d6e0f7b54cdd/pkg/cmd/project/item-list/item_list.go#L133-L142) checks the host and fails with "the `--query` flag is not supported on this GitHub host".
- The "If supported by the API host" wording stays to keep the diff small. `gh issue list`, `gh pr list`, and `gh search` say "On supported GitHub hosts" instead.
- Help that says a feature is "not supported on GitHub Enterprise Server" stays as is. That covers `@copilot` in `gh issue create`, `gh issue edit`, and `gh pr edit`, and semantic search in `gh search issues`. Those notes name no versions and explain why a documented value fails on GHES.

### Notes for reviewers

<!--
Where should review start, and what should be read next? Call out anything you are unsure about.

Link related issues or prior discussion, with one sentence on why each matters.
-->

The [#14519 review thread](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14519#discussion_r4107865905) asked to drop the same kind of host list from `gh search` help and pointed out this `item-list` instance.

### Authorship and follow-up

<!--
REQUIRED - If you are an AI agent filling in this template, answer "Who wrote this" for yourself and answer honestly. For "Who answers review comments," use only a choice the human has explicitly made in the conversation. If no choice has already been established, pause and ask the human to choose one of the three options before creating or updating the pull request. Do not infer the choice from repository ownership, authorship, assignees, prior interactions, or the current operator. After the human answers, check exactly the option they chose; the last option is valid when the human explicitly chooses nobody.

Check exactly one box in each list.
-->

Who wrote this:

- [ ] A human wrote it.
- [x] An agent wrote it under close human direction.
- [ ] An agent wrote it independently, and no human has guided the implementation beyond the initial prompt.

Who answers review comments:

- [x] @BagToad will read and reply directly.
- [ ] An agent will draft replies and @username will read them before they are posted.
- [ ] Nobody has explicitly committed to replying.

issue.body:
Created by `brew bump` --- Created with `brew bump-formula-pr`.
release notes 
## Security

Four security vulnerabilities have been identified, and fixed, in this release. Users are advised to update gh to version `v2.102.0` as soon as possible.

`gh release download`, `gh run download`, `gh repo read-file --output`, and `gh attestation download` could write remote content to an unintended local file when the destination contained symbolic links.

See https://github.com/cli/cli/security/advisories/GHSA-39wj-f2f4-978v for more information.

`gh attestation verify` compared the `--source-ref` value case-insensitively, so an attestation built from a branch whose name differs only in case could satisfy a policy that named a different branch.

See https://github.com/cli/cli/security/advisories/GHSA-4mq3-hpgx-9cx8 for more information.

Interactive `gh skill search` passed repository paths from search results to `gh skill install` without an option separator, so a search result could inject installer options and change where skill files were written.

See https://github.com/cli/cli/security/advisories/GHSA-qcwj-mr2r-2cx7 for more information.

`gh attestation verify` matched the `--signer-workflow` value against only the start of the signing certificate's identity, so an attestation signed by a different workflow in the pinned repository could pass verification when its path began with the pinned value.

See https://github.com/cli/cli/security/advisories/GHSA-wjmr-j3rp-mh2g for more information.

## What's Changed

### 🐛 Fixes

* Allow `ghu_` tokens for supported actors to attach files by @BagToad in [#14516](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14516)
* Allow repo set-default --unset without an argument by @williammartin in [#14540](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14540)

### 📚 Docs & Chores

* Prioritize HackerOne for vulnerability reports by @BagToad in [#14497](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14497)
* Clarify reviewer-facing PR guidance by @williammartin in [#14509](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14509)
* Add a skill for chaptered CLI recordings by @BagToad in [#14475](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14475)
* Improve CLI recording rendering by @williammartin in [#14507](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14507)
* Mention gh CLI in the README intro by @BagToad in [#14517](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14517)
* Document search operator support in `gh search` help by @waldyrious in [#14519](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14519)
* Remove host versions from `gh project item-list` help by @BagToad in [#14553](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14553)

### :dependabot: Dependencies

* chore(deps): bump the codeql-actions group with 3 updates by @dependabot in [#14486](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14486)
* chore(deps): bump nodeselector/setup-apple-codesign from 0.0.2 to 0.0.3 by @dependabot in [#14487](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14487)

Four security vulnerabilities have been identified, and fixed, in this release. Users are advised to update gh to version `v2.102.0` as soon as possible.

`gh release download`, `gh run download`, `gh repo read-file --output`, and `gh attestation download` could write remote content to an unintended local file when the destination contained symbolic links.

See https://github.com/cli/cli/security/advisories/GHSA-39wj-f2f4-978v for more information.

`gh attestation verify` compared the `--source-ref` value case-insensitively, so an attestation built from a branch whose name differs only in case could satisfy a policy that named a different branch.

See https://github.com/cli/cli/security/advisories/GHSA-4mq3-hpgx-9cx8 for more information.

Interactive `gh skill search` passed repository paths from search results to `gh skill install` without an option separator, so a search result could inject installer options and change where skill files were written.

See https://github.com/cli/cli/security/advisories/GHSA-qcwj-mr2r-2cx7 for more information.

`gh attestation verify` matched the `--signer-workflow` value against only the start of the signing certificate's identity, so an attestation signed by a different workflow in the pinned repository could pass verification when its path began with the pinned value.

See https://github.com/cli/cli/security/advisories/GHSA-wjmr-j3rp-mh2g for more information.

## What's Changed

### 🐛 Fixes

* Allow `ghu_` tokens for supported actors to attach files by @​BagToad in [#14516](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14516)
* Allow repo set-default --unset without an argument by @​williammartin in [#14540](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14540)

issue.body:
Adds **Link Hovercards** (`link-hovercards`).

## What it does

Hover a GitHub pull request, GitHub issue or Linear issue link anywhere in BB and a card shows what it points at:

- **Pull requests:** state (open, draft, merged, closed), title, description excerpt, base ← head, CI check tally, review decision, merge conflicts, labels, lines added and removed, files changed, author, last activity.
- **GitHub issues:** open, closed or not planned, labels, comments, assignees.
- **Linear issues:** workflow state, priority, project and cycle, due date, labels, assignee, linked PR count.

On touch screens, a long-press opens the card and a normal tap still follows the link. Moving the pointer into the card keeps it open. The card follows its link while a live thread scrolls.

## Source

- Repository: https://github.com/bborn/bb-plugin-link-hovercards (public, MIT)
- Entry source: `git` with range `^0.1.0`. Releases are tagged `v0.1.0`, `v0.1.1` and `v0.1.2`. v0.1.2 requires BB `>=0.44` and plugin SDK `>=0.5.29`. The plugin sits at the repository root.

## Plugin checks

- 19 vitest tests pass. They cover GitHub PR and issue parsing against real `gh` output, link detection, Linear key-to-workspace selection, Linear query errors and description excerpts.
- `tsc --noEmit` passes.
- `bb plugin build` passes. A fresh clone with production dependencies only also builds.
- Installed from `git:https://github.com/bborn/bb-plugin-link-hovercards.git@semver:^0.1.0`. PR and issue cards were checked live on desktop and in a touch emulation.
- On the released BB 0.44.0 (`bb-app@0.44.0`, SDK 0.5.29), `@v0.1.2` installs, runs, returns PR and issue cards through the host entry, and its overlay opens a card on hover. The plugin typechecks against `@get-bb/plugin-sdk@0.5.29`.
- The Linear GraphQL queries pass Linear's schema validation. A live Linear card hasn't been checked with a key yet.

## Marketplace checks

- `npm run build` passes, with 256 entries.
- `npm run check` passes. The remaining warning is about an existing, unrelated entry with no category.
- `git diff --check` is clean.

## Permissions, services and security

- **Surfaces:** registers one `experimental_appOverlay` for the cards and a host entry (`bb.host`) that runs `gh pr view` and `gh api` on the BB server's machine. It adds no CLI commands, agent tools or background services.
- **GitHub:** needs the GitHub CLI signed in on the server's machine. Cards show what that account can see.
- **Linear:** optional. Reads go to `https://api.linear.app/graphql` with personal API keys held in a `secret: true` setting. The keys stay on the server and never reach the frontend.
- **Writes:** none, to GitHub or to Linear. The plugin stores nothing beyond an in-memory cache: one minute for answers and ten seconds for errors.

## Screenshots

Both show the real plugin over BB's built-in Markdown preview of a note that links only to public `cli/cli` items:

1. `pull-request.png`: the card for cli/cli#14519, showing open state, branches, 11 checks passed, "Changes requested", labels and diff size.
2. `issue.png`: the card for cli/cli#14529, showing open state, description excerpt, labels and comment count.
